questions.explain: The outbox pattern writes the event record into a table in the same transaction as the business data change, so the event is guaranteed to exist if and only if the business transaction committed — atomicity without distributed coordination.
options: Duplicate event delivery when two relay workers run concurrently
Lost events when the database commits but the message broker write fails
Events that exist without a committed business transaction, and vice versa
Slow CDC capture jobs when the outbox table has no index
questions.q: What is the dual-write problem that the transactional outbox pattern solves?

questions.explain: CDC encodes deletes as 1, inserts as 2, before-update images as 3, and after-update images as 4 — so an update appears as a before/after pair of rows.
options: The after-update image of an updated row
A tombstone event for a deleted row
The before-update image of an updated row
An insert of a new row
questions.q: In SQL Server CDC change tables, what does __$operation = 4 represent?

questions.explain: Service Broker automatically moves a message that has been rolled back five times to a dead letter queue — its built-in poison-message handling, which you must design an explicit inspection path around.
options: One rollback — the message is discarded immediately
Three rollbacks — matching the outbox retry_count convention
Five rollbacks
Ten rollbacks, with exponential backoff between each
questions.q: After how many rollbacks does SQL Server Service Broker automatically move a message to its dead letter queue?

questions.explain: UPDLOCK + READPAST lets multiple relay workers run concurrently: each worker locks the rows it reads and skips rows already locked by another session, partitioning the work without explicit coordination.
options: WITH (NOLOCK, READUNCOMMITTED) so workers never block on each other
WITH (UPDLOCK, READPAST) so workers lock their rows and skip rows locked by others
WITH (TABLOCK, HOLDLOCK) so exactly one worker processes at a time
WITH (SERIALIZABLE) and a global application lock per worker
questions.q: How should multiple concurrent outbox relay workers read unprocessed rows without contending for the same rows?

questions.explain: The CDC cleanup job's retention is configured with sp_cdc_change_job using @job_type = 'cleanup' and @retention in minutes (4320 = 72 hours), with @threshold limiting rows deleted per cycle.
options: ALTER DATABASE OrdersDB SET CDC_RETENTION = 72 HOURS
sp_cdc_change_job with @job_type = 'cleanup' and @retention = 4320 (minutes)
DBCC FREEPROCCACHE with a 72-hour plan cache eviction policy
sp_cdc_enable_db with @retention_window = '72:00:00'
questions.q: How is SQL Server CDC cleanup retention configured, and what does 4320 mean in the chapter's example?
